chunks: Abu Baṣīr narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
"Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, surely calls out every Thursday night from above His Throne, from the beginning of the night until its end:

Is there not a believing servant who calls upon Me for his Hereafter and his worldly life before the rising of dawn, so that I may answer him? Is there not a believing servant who repents to Me from his sins before the rising of dawn, so that I may turn to him? Is there not a believing servant whose provision I have constrained, and he asks Me for increase in his provision before the rising of dawn, so that I may expand it for him? Is there not a believing servant who is ill and asks Me to heal him before the rising of dawn, so that I may grant him well-being? Is there not a believing servant, imprisoned and distressed, who asks Me to release him from his confinement, so that I may set him free? Is there not a believing servant who is wronged and asks Me to take for him his due from the wrong done to him before the rising of dawn, so that I may grant him victory and take for him his due from the wrong done to him?
He said: He continues calling out this way until dawn rises."

key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn, the endpoint mentioned for this divine call
key_terms.سَقِيمٌ: one who is ill or sick
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ جُمُعَةٍ: the night of Jumuʿah, a specially blessed time

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the virtue of making du'a on Thursday night before dawn?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the special mercy of Allah on the night of Jumuʿah, when He calls His believing servants to supplication, tawbah, and seeking relief before dawn. It emphasizes divine response to du'a for religious and worldly needs, forgiveness, expanded provision, healing, release from distress, and justice for the oppressed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1239 - Abu Basir narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:
"Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, calls out every Thursday night (the night of Jumu’ah) from above His Throne, from the beginning of the night until its end:

'Is there not a believing servant who calls upon Me concerning his Hereafter and his worldly life before the break of dawn so that I may answer him?
Is there not a believing servant who repents to Me from his sins before the break of dawn so that I may accept his repentance?
Is there not a believing servant upon whom I have tightened his provision who asks Me for an increase in his provision before the break of dawn so that I may expand it for him?
Is there not a believing servant who is sick and asks Me to heal him before the break of dawn so that I may grant him health?
Is there not a believing servant who is imprisoned or in distress who asks Me to release him from his confinement so that I may free him?
Is there not a believing servant who is wronged and asks Me to avenge his oppression before the break of dawn so that I may grant him justice?'
The call continues until the break of dawn."
